paper.summary: An efficient method to determine absolute nuclear charge radii from high-precision bound-electron g-factor measurements in hydrogenlike ions is put forward. Assuming that a nuclear model independent radius determination is possible, we demonstrate that this method can improve the precision of the nuclear radius for several poorly known heavy isotopes by up to two orders of magnitude compared to current literature values, by utilizing recent breakthroughs in the quantum electrodynamics (QED) theory of the bound-electron g-factor [B. Sikora, V. A. Yerokhin, C. H. Keitel, and Z. Harman, Phys. Rev. Lett. 134, 123001 (2025)]. This opens a new, independent pathway for testing nuclear structure models and resolving nuclear structure anomalies.

paper.title: Maximal correlation and optimal transformations of probability distributions in tensor-train format: a variational algorithm
paper.summary: The correlation between two subsystems $A$ and $B$ of a many-body system is usually measured through a pair of observables chosen in advance. The Hirschfeld-Gebelein-Rényi maximal correlation removes the choice: it is the largest correlation coefficient between any function of the configuration of $A$ and any function of the configuration of $B$, and the two functions that reach it, the optimal transformations, are the observables that carry the correlation. Both follow from a singular value decomposition (SVD) of the joint distribution normalized by its marginals, a matrix whose dimension is the number of configurations. We show that this SVD can be computed variationally for a classical distribution of discrete variables, such as the Boltzmann distribution of a spin model, given in the tensor-train (matrix-product) format, without ever forming the matrix. The optimal transformations are sought as tensor trains; each step updates a single core in closed form, and the inverse of a small matrix contracted from the distribution and the remaining cores performs the division by the marginals core by core. Every iterate is a feasible pair, so the objective is a lower bound on the maximal correlation that increases monotonically, and the cost grows linearly with the number of variables. The algorithm reproduces the exact SVD on small systems, recovers the known nonlinear optimal transformations of synthetic distributions of up to ten angular variables ($10^{15}$ configurations), and, for the bipartite antiferromagnetic model with $2^{32}$ configurations, returns an optimal transformation that is a function of the group magnetization, linear above the transition and sign-like below it: the staggered order parameter is read off from the distribution instead of being postulated.

paper.title: A physics-informed neural network method for pressure-driven turbine-blade optimization
paper.summary: We develop a physics-informed method for aerodynamic shape optimisation of turbine blades, treating the flow field and blade geometry as coupled unknowns. The method translates prescribed surface-pressure distributions into geometric modifications through pressure-target continuation and alternating flow-geometry updates. A differentiable representation of the blade surfaces allows their positions and orientations to be optimised within the current flow field, followed by flow re-adaptation to the modified boundaries. The inverse formulation uses the two-dimensional steady compressible Euler equations as physics constraints and is evaluated on the LS89 turbine cascade using 28 pressure-target points derived from experimental data. Starting from a modified profile and a warm-started flow network, the final pressure-side and suction-side root-mean-square fitting errors are 1.13% and 2.21% of inlet total pressure, respectively. Independent forward verification with SharC reproduces the principal surface-pressure trends of the experimental measurements, with remaining differences near the trailing edge. These results demonstrate the translation of experimental-origin loading data into geometric blade modifications through coordinated optimisation of the flow field and moving boundaries.

paper.title: BIC-Engineered Silicon Nitride Microring Resonators Enabled by an Etch-Free Laser-Writing Approach
paper.summary: We report the initial experimental demonstration of a complementary, etch-free approach with fewer fabrication steps, in useful SU-8 ridges written by direct ultraviolet laser lithography on an unpatterned silicon nitride film define waveguides and microring resonators. Because the nitride film is never patterned, scattering at patterned nitride sidewalls does not arise, and the remaining radiative loss is engineered by design. The guided transverse-magnetic mode lies within the continuum of transverse-electric slab modes, and we use bound states in the continuum (BICs) as a design tool to control this radiation. Coupled-mode analysis and full-vectorial simulations show that radiation from the two ridge sidewalls cancels by destructive interference at discrete widths, with a first BIC at 2.25 micron and radiation below 1 dB/cm over a 0.3 micron width window and about 200 nm of bandwidth, and that curvature confines this cancellation to discrete bands of bending radius and width. Laser-written waveguides follow the predicted width dependence of the loss, reaching approximately 1.5 dB/cm near the BIC, where non-radiative loss dominates. A microring designed on a radius-selected BIC band exhibits loaded quality factors up to 1.6 \times 10^4 and, under the over-coupled assignment supported by a coupler model, an intrinsic quality factor of 3.3 \times 10^5. Because radiation is set by a patterned low-index layer on an unetched film, the same approach could be extended to other nanostructures. Optimization of the writing conditions and materials is ongoing.

paper.title: The preplasma origin of the plasma-mirror reflectivity response
paper.summary: Plasma mirrors (PM) enhance the temporal contrast of high-power lasers, but declining reflectivity at subrelativistic intensities limits their energy throughput. Here we show that prepulse-generated preplasma drives this decline in p polarization primarily through absorption. Particle-in-cell simulations using a measured prepulse profile reproduce the reflectivity decrease, with near- and far-field energy accounting showing a weak contribution from scattering. Optical-cycle-resolved electron tracking reveals successive electron bunches extracted from the plasma surface, supporting a vacuum-heating interpretation. Under the simulated conditions, s-polarized absorption remains weak and no comparable decline occurs. Applying the model to two representative double-plasma-mirror (DPM) systems, BELLA and CoReLS, it captures both the p-polarized and s-polarized reflectivity responses across the operating range. Yet, the model still misses the high-fluence s-polarized reflectivity rollover, and further investigation of the scattering channel might be needed. These findings connect prepulse history to polarization-dependent energy loss, informing the choice of plasma-mirror operating conditions.

paper.title: Finesse evolution in a bichromatic cavity under blue and red resonant illumination in vacuum
paper.summary: The long-term performance of high-finesse optical cavities depends on the stability of their mirror coatings under vacuum and under continuous exposure to high circulating power. In cavities supporting multiple wavelengths, a central question is whether degradation at one wavelength compromises performance at another. Understanding this interplay is essential for those cavity quantum electrodynamics experiments that need diverse optical fields for cavity stabilization, trapping, and light--matter coupling. Here, we investigate wavelength-dependent degradation and recovery of a bichromatic cavity with high-reflectivity coating at 455 nm and 671 nm in vacuum. Cavity ring-down measurements reveal a decrease in the 455 nm finesse from 7.7*10^3 to 1.9*10^3 after 11 hours of continuous exposure to high circulating power. Simultaneous measurements show no measurable degradation at 671 nm. Continuous operation at 671 nm, instead, produces no measurable degradation at either wavelength under the tested conditions. Comparison of oxygen depletion and Avrami-type loss models indicates kinetics compatible with nucleation and growth, without uniquely identifying the microscopic mechanism. We demonstrate partial recovery of the finesse with illumination at 455 nm in air. Our results indicate a wavelength dependence of laser-induced optical damage in bichromatic cavities and provide an estimate of the blue light intensity that can be safely used in such cavities.

paper.title: Quantum simulation of dissipative acoustic and elastic waves by Schrödingerisation: absorbing boundaries and explicit polynomial-size circuits
paper.summary: Explicit quantum circuits for the acoustic and elastic wave equations, obtained by Hamiltonian simulation of their first-order forms, conserve energy and therefore describe closed domains: an outgoing wave reflects off the edge of the computational region or, with periodic boundaries, wraps around and re-enters from the opposite side. We open the domain with the simplest physical absorber, a graded sponge layer in which every wave field is damped at a rate that grows towards the outer edge, and implement the resulting dissipative dynamics on a quantum simulator by Schrödingerisation, which turns a non-unitary linear evolution into a family of unitary ones by means of a single auxiliary variable. We derive the whole chain from the partial differential equation to the circuit, in one, two and three dimensions. An independent finite-difference solver confirms that damping all wave fields absorbs far better than the common velocity-only damping mask. For the sponge the quantum analysis is sharp: recovery is exact on the whole non- negative half of the auxiliary axis at every time; that axis can be truncated periodically at a length set by the largest damping rate and the simulated time; and the success probability is a fixed constant, about 0.4, times the fraction of the energy not yet absorbed, with only one or two auxiliary qubits measured. On the circuit side, the damping step, which generic synthesis compiles into a number of controlled-NOT gates exponential in the number of qubits, factorises exactly into polynomially many multi-controlled phase gates. Gate-level simulations on up to 25 qubits agree with the classical solutions of the damped wave equations.

paper.title: On the role of grazing atmospheric particles in hypersonic boundary-layer receptivity
paper.summary: The role of small atmospheric particulates in the initiation of the laminar-turbulent transition is investigated for the HIFLIER vehicle during Mach 6 ascent condition. High-fidelity simulations are used to examine the disturbance wavepackets generated by particles following either grazing trajectories through the boundary layer or trajectories that lead to impact and rebound at the cone surface. Grazing particles that penetrate less than halfway through the boundary layer are found to generate wavepackets with amplitudes comparable to those produced by wall-impinging particles. To identify the receptivity mechanisms responsible for this behaviour, a multiple-scales asymptotic formulation is developed that accounts for the extended streamwise region over which a particle interacts with the boundary layer. The analysis shows that a grazing particle can generate a strong disturbance response when crossing the critical layer, where the streamwise-momentum component of the adjoint mode is largest and the boundary layer is most receptive. Thus, direct surface impact is not required for atmospheric particulates to excite dynamically significant instability waves. Root-mean-square disturbance estimates for submicron grazing particles predict transition-onset locations close to those measured in flight, suggesting they may have contributed significantly to the onset of transition on HIFLIER at the trajectory condition considered.

paper.title: Colloidal 2D WS2 nanosheets exhibiting high-purity single photon emission
paper.summary: The search for quantum emitters, delivering single photons "on demand" at cryogenic and elevated temperatures for photonic technologies is ever progressing. For example, micrometer-sized WS2 monolayers exhibit single photon emission by elaborated local defect or strain engineering. Here, we show that wet-chemically synthesised monolayered two-dimensional (2D) WS2 nano sheets (NSs) with lateral sizes of 14 (+/- 6 nm) readily emit single photons from exciton recombination without the need for substrate-induced patterning, strain/defect engineering or spectral filtering. Single particle spectroscopy of 70 individual NSs shows photoluminescence from excitons (2.02 eV), trios (1.94 eV) and defect-localized states (1.85 eV) with fast emission (t1<0.2 ns, t2=3.2 ns), allowing highly frequent excitation cycles. Pulsed at 80 MHz, colloidal WS2 NSs exhibit limited spectral diffusion, no blinking and distinct photon antibunching (g2(0)=0.07 at 5 K), thereby tackling challenges of established colloidal quantum dot systems (blinking, longer emission cycles), while retaining high single photon purity as key quality of deterministic quantum emitters.

paper.title: Conceptual Design of Pumping Systems up to 1000 m3/s Based on Non-Evaporable Getters in a Gas-Dynamic Magnetic Trap
paper.summary: The Gas-Dynamic Magnetic Trap (GDMT), a new linear magnetic facility for confining high-temperature hydrogen plasma, is currently under development at the Budker Institute of Nuclear Physics (BINP SB RAS). The total hydrogen flow that must be removed from the end expanders by the vacuum system is approximately 10^22 molecules/s, which corresponds to a required pumping speed on the order of 500 m3/s. Non-evaporable getters (NEG) are considered as a possible pumping method for this application. This article presents experimental studies of Ti-Zr-Al getters manufactured by Polema LLC. The pumping speed, sorption capacity, and sticking factors of the getter surface were measured. The sticking factors for hydrogen and deuterium are 2.23% and 1.54%, respectively. The getter pumping speed is maintained over 60 air-vent/reactivation cycles. Based on these results, a conceptual design of a NEG-based pumping system for the GDMT end expanders is proposed, providing a specific pumping speed of 74 m3/(m3s) for the getter panel. The proposed pumping system design and the required heating power are discussed.

paper.title: Brillouin comb line amplifiers for optical atomic clocks
paper.summary: Optical atomic clocks outperform the microwave clocks at the heart of current timing and navigation infrastructure by orders-of-magnitude, and recent progress in on-chip integration provides the opportunity to widely deploy them. Conventionally, a narrow linewidth laser interrogates the atomic transition, and an optical frequency comb divides its stabilised frequency (hundreds of terahertz) down to a microwave that is electronically countable. The laser(s) impose a significant size, weight, power and cost penalty, which is a current barrier to low-cost, scalable, fully on-chip optical clocks. Here, we position the frequency comb as the central engine of the clock by using Brillouin-amplified comb lines for atomic spectroscopy, which eliminates the need for stable clock lasers. Amplified comb lines reach an ultra-low frequency noise floor of $6\,\mathrm{Hz^2/Hz}$ at $30\,\mathrm{kHz}$ offset, an order-of-magnitude below a high-end commercial fibre laser. We realize a clock based on the $\mathrm{5S}_{1/2}\rightarrow\mathrm{5D}_{5/2}$ transition in $^{87}\mathrm{Rb}$ with competitive fractional frequency stability of $2\times10^{-13}$ at $τ= 1\,\mathrm{s}$, averaging to $9\times10^{-15}$ at $τ= 1000\,\mathrm{s}$. Lastly, we demonstrate a photonic chip-integrated Brillouin amplifier with a record 62.9 dB gain and up to 40 dB transferred noise suppression when pumped with a simple, low-cost diode laser. This opens a new route to compact optical clocks and enables use of atomic transitions lacking low-noise lasers by broadening a comb to the required wavelength and amplifying single lines.

paper.title: Variational learning of energy-stable macroscopic flow equations from microscopic laws
paper.summary: We present a generalized variational approach for constructing energy-stable macroscopic partial differential equations (PDEs) directly from microscopic physical laws. Rather than fitting the PDE evolution for prescribed variables from macroscopic trajectories, we construct an extendable variational structure by adjoining auxiliary variables to seek autonomous reduced dynamics in an enlarged state space. By defining these variables as micro--macro encoders with explicit microscopic counterparts, we cast the learning problem as the sample-wise joint identification of the reduced state representation and the variational ingredients from time-discrete data, enabling systematic law-level transfer across scales. The resulting PDEs preserve frame indifference, physical constraints, and energy stability by construction, and admit a fluctuation--dissipation-consistent stochastic extension. Numerical results for the non-Newtonian hydrodynamics of polymeric fluids show that the learned models capture the viscoelastic responses induced by nonlinear and heterogeneous molecular interactions beyond empirical closures.

paper.title: Coupled Effects of Biofilm Dynamics and Flow on Hydrogen Transport in a Hydrogen-Generating Fracture
paper.summary: Biofilm growth in hydrogen-generating fractures modifies fluid flow and hydrogen transport, while microbial activity consumes hydrogen. These coupled processes influence hydrogen recovery in stimulated geologic hydrogen systems. We use high-fidelity simulations to investigate flow, biofilm dynamics, and hydrogen transport in a rough fracture with reactive walls. Flow rate and biofilm permeability were varied to quantify changes in fracture permeability, biomass accumulation, and outlet hydrogen concentration. Biofilm growth reduced apparent fracture permeability by up to 65\% as biomass occupied the aperture. Two hydrogen concentration regimes are identified. For highly permeable biofilms (Type I), outlet concentration evolved non-monotonically as roughness-induced vortices initially restricted hydrogen transport before biofilm growth suppressed them. Low-permeability biofilms (Type II) result in an approximately monotonic outlet concentration decrease dominated by transport resistance and microbial consumption. The regimes were distinguished by a Darcy-scale Reynolds number ($Re_D=u\sqrt{K_0}/ν$). Temporal hydrogen concentration variations in field studies may help determine intrinsic biofilm permeability.

paper.title: Millimeter-Wave Gaussian-to-Flat-Top Beam Shaping Using a Single-Curvature Lens: A Novel Approach
paper.summary: This paper presents a novel method for converting the divergent Gaussian intensity distribution of a millimeter-wave source into a uniform (flat-top) distribution using a single curved surface. The proposed method combines the surface profile of a collimator with that of a beam shaper. To validate the method, the profile of a single-sided (plano-convex) lens is derived and placed 52 mm in front of a conical horn antenna operating at 100 GHz. The lens transforms the Gaussian radiation of the horn, with an incident beam radius of 11.9 mm, into a uniform beam with a radius of 400 mm at a distance of 3 m. The lens surface profile is optimized using a full-wave-simulation-based procedure, and the resulting output beam is compared with that of a previously designed double-sided (concave-convex) lens. Simulation results show that, within the desired field of view, the optimized single-sided lens produces a flat-top intensity distribution with satisfactory ripple and roll-off. Finally, the sensitivity of the optimized lens to frequency variation is investigated. The proposed lens is suitable for generating uniform illumination in active stand-off millimeter-wave imaging systems.

paper.title: A Two-Dimensional Physics-Informed Neural Network Model of a Hall Effect Thruster Plasma: Self-Consistent Electrostatics and Physical-Consistency Diagnostics
paper.summary: We present a two-dimensional axisymmetric physics-informed neural network (PINN) of the discharge channel of the P5 Hall thruster at 300 V and 5.4 A, which solves eleven coupled plasma fields and assimilates 145 internal probe measurements per field reconstructed from the data of Haas and Gallimore. The electric potential is obtained from Poisson's equation in charge-separation form, n_e = n_i(1+eta), with eta bounded by construction, which keeps the stiff electrostatic constraint active and trainable. The reference solution agrees with the training profiles to relative L2 errors of 0.017, 0.073 and 0.205 for the potential, electron temperature and ion density, and held-out tests show the potential to be far more robust than the ion density to the withdrawal of measurement lines. We then test the solution against requirements the data fit does not reveal: global particle and current balances, the electron current implied by the momentum equation, the field-aligned electron force balance and the axial ion momentum budget. These expose a neutral inflow six times the measured flow, a bound in the potential representation, and a momentum-implied electron current, more than 99% field-aligned, exceeding the discharge current by orders of magnitude. Correcting these, with a divergence-free magnetic field fitted to measured data, uncertainty-weighted data, the electron pressure gradient and progressively imposed field-aligned and current constraints, yields a solution that conserves particles to within 3%, holds the current between 5.1 and 5.4 A and places 97% of the potential and 88% of the temperature measurements within their uncertainties. Within the tested single-velocity fluid formulation, however, the ion density, potential and ion velocity could not be matched together, and the field-aligned electron balance remains the main obstacle to electron self-consistency.

paper.title: Inducing cooperative dynamics in an inhomogeneous many-emitter ensemble with a pulse sequence
paper.summary: Driving a many-particle quantum system with an appropriately tuned external field can give rise to features in its nonequilibrium dynamics that are absent in the equilibrium counterpart. Cooperative dynamics in a dense ensemble of quantum emitters manifested through superradiance, a burst in the emission intensity as a function of time, is typically suppressed by spectral disparities among emitters in the ensemble. We demonstrate the enhancement of cooperative dynamics in a spectrally inhomogeneous ensemble of quantum emitters when it is driven by a periodic pulse sequence. Using both a semi-analytical mean-field solution and a digital quantum simulation, we examine the coherence of the pulse-driven ensemble and the intensity of the emitted radiation as a function of the spectral disparity in the ensemble, as a function of time, the number of atoms in the system, and as a function of the inter-pulse delay. We identify clear signatures of the enhanced cooperative dynamics for the pulse-driven inhomogeneous ensemble when dephasing in the dynamics of the ensemble is suppressed by a sufficient number of pulses during the individual emitter lifetime. These results demonstrate a post-fabrication tuning knob based on externally applied control fields for the dynamics of the many-emitter ensemble.

paper.title: Quantum HHL Algorithm for Solving 1D Linear Advection Equation Using Explicit and Implicit Finite Difference Schemes
paper.summary: This study develops and implements a Harrow-Hassidim-Lloyd (HHL) quantum algorithm for solving a one-dimensional linear advection equation with periodic boundary conditions. The governing equation is first discretized using a classical finite difference (FD) scheme to obtain a linear system suitable for quantum solution. We present a newly designed, circuit-level implementation of HHL assembled from Qiskit circuit components and exploit the circulant structure of the periodic discretization matrices through Fourier-based matrix evolution. The HHL algorithm is benchmarked with three explicit schemes and one implicit scheme. The implicit scheme requires a nontrivial linear solve arising from the discretized PDE on progressively finer grids, whereas the explicit schemes provide different input fields for testing state preparation and reconstruction with identity coefficient matrices. HHL solution states are validated against direct classical solves in noiseless simulation. For hardware execution, the periodic matrix structure permits a Fourier implementation that applies reciprocal eigenvalues without phase estimation. Results on the IBM Rensselaer Nighthawk processor are compared at a shared final time. Noiseless reconstructed fields approach the transported profile on resolved grids, while substantial hardware errors remain for both explicit and implicit schemes. Crank-Nicolson remains exceptionally well-conditioned and utilizes similar circuit re sources to the explicit controls, proving that hardware degradation in our tests was not driven by poor matrix conditioning. Ultimately, this study shows new means for HHL algorithms to study quantum CFD problems involving advection equations with implicit time integrations, while demonstrating how state preparation and measurement affect the practical performance of quantum solvers on current devices.

paper.title: Improving the performance of regularized Stokeslet simulations using Rosenbrock time integration methods
paper.summary: The method of regularized Stokeslets (MRS) is widely used to model fluid-structure interactions of microscopic bodies in viscous environments. Specifically, MRS computes the fluid velocity generated by regularized forces distributed on an immersed body, which in turn defines a system of ordinary differential equations with which to evolve the body so that the no-slip condition is enforced. To accurately model material properties such as elasticity and bending rigidity, the resulting ODE system is often stiff and, therefore, computationally expensive to solve with explicit time-integration methods. Here we demonstrate the potential of linearly implicit Rosenbrock (ROS) time integration methods to greatly reduce the computational time required to solve such ODE systems. We focus on the classic model problem of the swimming of a flexible filament driven by preferred curvature forcing. Our findings indicate that, compared to previous MRS simulations, the increased stability of ROS methods allows for speed-ups between twenty and two thousand times over explicit Runge-Kutta (ERK) methods. Moreover, we present approximate scaling laws for this speedup as a function of the key model parameters (bending rigidity and slenderness) at the root of numerical stiffness. Lastly, beyond the basic ROS approach, we discuss several additional strategies that further improve performance.

paper.title: Single-sided lens terahertz flat-top beam shaping in the Fresnel region
paper.summary: In this paper, a novel, to our knowledge, analytical approach is introduced for the design of a single-sided plano-convex lens (PCL) capable of terahertz (THz) flat-top beam shaping in the Fresnel region. The lens profile, derived from geometrical optics principles, integrates collimating and beam-shaping functions into a single optical surface, thereby simplifying fabrication. The efficiency of the method is demonstrated by designing two PCLs that convert a divergent Gaussian beam from a monochromatic THz source (at 100 and 200 GHz) into flat-top beams with target radii of 400 and 500 mm at distances of 3 and 4 m, respectively. The resulting fields, evaluated through analytical, integral equation, and finite element techniques, are shown to be comparable to those produced by a conventional double-sided concave-convex lens. Furthermore, the sensitivity of the design to frequency and alignment variations is investigated, confirming the robustness of this single-curvature approach for integration into practical THz imaging systems.

paper.title: Dynamics of Vortex Electrons in a Uniform Magnetic Field Across Nonrelativistic and Relativistic Regimes
paper.summary: The dynamics of a vortex electron in a transverse uniform magnetic field involves not only the cyclotron motion of the wave packet center but also the evolution of its internal wavefunction structure. To study this process, we develop a quantum framework and investigate the dynamics of vortex electrons in both the nonrelativistic and relativistic regimes. A discrete Bessel-Gaussian initial wave packet is expanded in the basis of Dirac eigenstates to obtain the time-dependent wavefunction and to analyze its spatiotemporal evolution. In the nonrelativistic regime, the results deviate significantly from the rigid point-dipole model, as the intrinsic kinetic orbital angular momentum exhibits dynamics more complex than simple Larmor precession, owing to the nonstationary internal current distribution of the wave packet. In the relativistic regime, the nonlinear dependence of the energy levels on the quantum numbers destroys the equal spacing of the spectrum. Consequently, the relative phases among the eigenstate components of the wave packet evolve nonuniformly, resulting in wave-packet spreading and deformation, accompanied by modified intrinsic orbital angular momentum dynamics. We introduce a dimensionless parameter to quantify this relativistic dephasing, providing an approximate criterion for selecting physical parameters and evolution times to mitigate the resulting wave-packet distortion. These results clarify the limitations of the rigid point-dipole model, highlight the essential role of internal wavefunction structure, and provide theoretical guidance for understanding and manipulating relativistic vortex electrons.

paper.title: Pump-scheme dependence of few-emitter lasers: exact multilevel correlations and photon statistics
paper.summary: Few-emitter laser models usually replace the excitation cycle of the gain medium by a single Markovian pump jump of a two-level emitter. We test this replacement with the cavity and laser-transition parameters held fixed and the two-level pump rate fitted to the same mean photon number, using an exact damping-basis continued-fraction solution of the cavity--emitter master equation for $N$ identical $d$-level emitters with arbitrary independent incoherent transitions and one cavity-coupled transition, in the known reduced space of level populations and lasing coherences. First, a pump-quantum filtration shows that the inter-emitter coherence of $Λ$ and ladder media starts at second rather than first order in the pump; we evaluate its leading coefficient from the exact finite-system series and map the recycling rate at which its sign changes. Second, at matched photon number, rate-limited steps in the pump cycle push the long-time output-counting Fano factor of two and three emitters well below one: for two emitters it reaches 0.66 at a mean cavity occupation of 0.3 and is still 0.74 at an occupation of one, where $g^{(2)}(0)$ is within 3% of unity, because the anticorrelation sits at delays of about half a cavity lifetime rather than at zero delay. For two and three emitters the fitted two-level model gets both statistics wrong and places the output above the shot-noise level. Against independent single-emitter lasers at the same output, the common cavity erodes rather than enhances this single-emitter effect.

paper.title: Structure-Preserving Full Approximation Scheme for Real-Space Hartree-Fock Equations
paper.summary: We develop a structure-preserving full approximation scheme (FAS) for the real-space restricted Hartree-Fock equations. The method treats the orbital equations, Coulomb and exchange pair potentials, and orthonormality constraints as a coupled nonlinear system on a hierarchy of finite-element spaces. Forced Gram targets, occupied-frame alignment, and auxiliary-variable reconstruction provide constraint compatibility and occupied-rotation equivariance under suitable assumptions. Analysis of the full self-consistent response identifies an elliptic kinetic principal part, motivating the multilevel treatment. The resulting solver, FAS-H, combines FAS cycles with a residual-triggered horizontal Newton correction on the finest grid. Numerical experiments on eight closed-shell systems show convergence in 4-11 cycles across three grid levels. Across 24 system-grid comparisons, FAS-H is 1.60-5.02 times faster than SCF and uses 68-91% less weighted FFT work, while standalone horizontal Newton is faster in some cases.

paper.title: The kinematic Kelvin-Helmholtz instability-driven dynamo: implications for merging compact objects
paper.summary: Binary neutron star (BNS) mergers excite a Kelvin--Helmholtz instability (KHI) in the shear layer between them. It is parasitized upon by the magnetic field to form a powerful magnetic dynamo. Using a large ensemble of high-resolution visco-resistive KHI-driven dynamo simulations we construct analytical, asymptotic in Reynolds number ($\rm{Re}$) models for the magnetic field growth rates and mean vertical field dynamo onset times. Our models suggest that in the $\rm{Re} \gg 1$ limit, the mean vertical field is seeded immediately, kinematic growth rates become asymptotic in $\rm{Re}$, and the dynamo moves out of the kinematic stage on $\mathcal{O}(0.1\,\rm{ms})$ timescales, readily attaining magnetar-strength fields during this transition. This suggests that most global BNS merger simulations are not time-resolving the correct KHI-driven dynamo regime.

paper.title: Optical angular momentum and pseudospin-orbit coupling in photonic graphene
paper.summary: We investigate the dynamics of structured laser beams carrying angular momentum (AM) as they undergo conical diffraction in photonic graphene. Using a combination of numerical simulations and analytical calculations, we demonstrate a surprising result: the beam's orbital AM tracks the dynamics of the lattice pseudospin rather than the AM of its slowly varying envelope. This finding provides evidence that pseudospin behaves as a genuine form of angular momentum. Furthermore, we explore beam propagation in staggered honeycomb lattices governed by the massive Dirac equation, revealing that the orbital AM is highly sensitive to both the band gap size and the envelope's initial AM. We explain our numerical results by drawing an analogy with the orbital magnetization of electrons.

paper.title: Stabilization of kinetic plasma instabilities via instantaneous external field control
paper.summary: We propose an instantaneous control framework for the stabilization of kinetic plasma instabilities using external fields. The control problem is formulated as a PDE-constrained optimization that accounts for nonlinear plasma dynamics, while the control is determined at each time step to avoid global-in-time optimization. The Discretize-then-Optimize (DtO) approach is adopted, with the forward equations first discretized using a particle-in-cell (PIC) method. The subsequent control computation is derived from the discrete particle update, ensuring consistency with the forward solver. The control objective is formulated in terms of electromagnetic field energy and low-order moments rather than the full distribution function, making the optimization more amenable to practical implementation. The framework is applied to both electrostatic and electromagnetic settings and evaluated on several benchmark problems, including the two-stream, bump-on-tail, Dory--Guest--Harris, and Weibel instabilities. Across these tests, the control successfully suppresses field energy growth and keeps the distribution function close to its initial state. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed strategy in suppressing kinetic plasma instabilities.

paper.title: Reversibility of Nonequilibrium Dynamics in a Unitary Fermi Gas
paper.summary: We theoretically describe and experimentally observe the reversibility of a nonequilibrium state in a unitary Fermi gas confined in a time-dependent trap. Unlike the equilibrium case, reversibility out of equilibrium imposes a stringent condition: the accumulated dynamical phase must be an integer multiple of $2π$, i.e., $Δφ= 2ω_{0} s(T) = 2nπ$, where $ω_{0}$ is the initial trapping frequency and $s(T)$ is the rescaled time after a total evolution time $T$. We demonstrate the reversibility of an initial nonequilibrium state in an isotropic unitary Fermi gas by driving the optical trap through a round trip. We find two types of reversible pathways, the space-time scaling-invariant and polynomial shortcut-to-adiabaticity (STA) protocols. The phase condition restricts the round-trip time $T$ to discrete values, a distinguishing feature of nonequilibrium dynamics. Our work establishes a clear criterion for the quantum control of nonequilibrium many-body systems beyond linear response and provides practical pathways to reversibility.

paper.title: ROSE: Deep Learning exchange-correlation functional from reduced density-matrix representations
paper.summary: We introduce ROSE, a deep-learning exchange--correlation energy functional built from the occupied-state density matrix. On GMTKN55 and on additional external benchmarks considered in this work, ROSE improves over modern neural network functionals trained under matched protocols and is on average more accurate than, or on par with, most hybrid and range-separated hybrid functionals considered here. On the experimental benchmarks considered here it has leading accuracy across hybrids, range separated hybrids, and neural functionals. These results motivate nonlocal density-matrix representations as a route to systematic improvement of learned XC functionals with low computational cost.

paper.title: Readable Is Not Steerable: Pre-Registered Tests of Physical Structure in Learned Fluid Representations
paper.summary: Self-supervised world models are often said to organize their latents around physical quantities. We test this on 2D decaying Navier-Stokes flow in three pre-registered studies, each tested once on held-out data. In Study 1, a joint-embedding predictive architecture (JEPA) trained to predict the flow fails the pre-registered criteria for organizing its latent around fluid quantities better than an untrained network of the same architecture (not supported); a JEPA trained on non-physical linear dynamics and a static invariance model that never sees time do as well or better. In Study 2, plain autoencoders that render the field make enstrophy prominent in their slowest unsupervised latent directions (best r 0.80-0.86 vs 0.38 untrained; fresh seeds, sealed data). Adding VICReg lowers this prominence in every comparison, though not by the pre-registered margin for vorticity, while raising the autoencoders' linear decodability (partially supported). In Study 3, we build steerable directions ("dials") by routing: the decoder gets overall scale only through a small conditioning code, while its other pathway carries a degraded copy of spectral shape. Label-free rules find a loudness dial in all 8 trained models and a shape dial in 3 of 5 fresh seeds on sealed data, against a pre-registered bar of 4; neither control shows a shape dial (partially supported). Across the studies, what a latent contains and what can be controlled through it come apart. In exploration, a supervised direction reading spectral shape almost perfectly moved nothing when steered. During the build, the loudness dial had to be found by its effect on the output (closest to a pure rescaling), not by data variance; for shape, a variance rule and an effect-constrained rule each worked in 3 of 5 seeds. The program used about 70 logged hours on one consumer GPU; all pre-registrations, deviations, code and outputs are public.

paper.title: Time-resolved infrared spectroscopy with entangled photons and visible-light detection
paper.summary: Time-resolved infrared (TR-IR) spectroscopy reveals molecular structural changes and charge-carrier dynamics on their intrinsic timescales, in photosynthesis, catalysis and optoelectronic materials, but requires complex sources of ultrashort infrared pulses, cryogenically cooled detectors to overcome thermal background, and intense probes that can perturb the sample. Quantum infrared spectroscopy avoids these constraints: harnessing quantum interference between the generation processes of frequency-entangled photon pairs, it reads out the infrared response of a sample by detecting only the visible partner photon, for which efficient detectors exist. To date, it has been limited to steady-state measurements. Here we demonstrate its ultrafast, time-resolved form with a picosecond visible pump pulse and a silicon detector. Each visible pulse generates photon pairs within a picosecond window; the infrared photon of a pair probes the excited sample at a set delay after excitation, and the transient response is read out from the count rate of its visible partner. We resolve picosecond carrier dynamics in a semiconductor saturable absorber mirror near 1529 nm with a picowatt-level probe, unaffected by thermal background and by sample IR photoluminescence 50 times stronger than the probe. The approach is applicable to the mid-infrared, fingerprint region, where infrared detection is hardest, and to the terahertz region.

paper.title: From Forecasting to Feedback: Evaluating Learned Dynamics for Tokamak Control
paper.summary: Learned temporal models are moving beyond offline forecasting toward interactive environments for decision making, yet logged-trajectory accuracy need not predict closed-loop behavior under policies optimized in the learned model. This forecasting-control gap matters in tokamak magnetic control, where coupled plasma-circuit dynamics and actuator constraints can amplify errors through feedback. Using a calibrated free-boundary Grad-Shafranov solver, we collect four datasets in a 2x2 design over physics-parameter and current-reference coverage. At matched budgets of 500, 1k, 3k, and 5k rollouts, we train 16 action-conditioned Transformers; PPO policies optimized in the 5k surrogates are then evaluated without adaptation on six reference-solver conditions. Only joint-coverage D4 shows monotonically decreasing cross-condition mean error, whereas D1 improves in distribution but degrades out of distribution. Binary completion masks substantial closed-loop differences: D2-D4 each complete 83.3% of conditions, but reach on average 99.0%, 94.7%, and 90.5% of the evaluation horizon, while their worst conditions reach 94.2%, 68.2%, and 43.2%. Policies trained with action noise complete 5/24 matched conditions, compared with 19/24 under nominal training, and have a lower mean horizon-capped episode length. Based on one trained policy per configuration and one evaluation realization per condition, the results support combining prediction error, episode completion, condition-level duration, and tracking quality.

paper.title: The Valence and Inner Shell Ionization Properties of Sr I - III by Non-Thermal Electrons in Kilonovae
paper.summary: The presence of strontium (Z = 38) was identified from spectra of the first multi-messenger kilonova transient, AT2017gfo, with the evolution of its spectral signature indicating a rapidly changing ionization balance. Interpretation of spectra at later times requires a more detailed understanding of recombination and ionization processes, including ionization by `non-thermal' electrons produced by beta decay. Published measurements of the ionization cross sections of Sr I and Sr II show complex structures likely arising from excitation autoionization. Using the Flexible Atomic Code we report calculations of the valence and inner shell ionization cross sections for Sr I, Sr II, and Sr III, and recover similar structures in the ionization cross sections. Though no measurements exist for Sr III, the calculations suggest negligible contributions from excitation autoionization. These new data are incorporated into Spencer-Fano models of non-thermal electron degradation and coupled to an ionization balance solver. The effects of excitation autoionization, treated as excitation with the additional production of an Auger electron, on the degradation spectra of non-thermal are explored. Calculations at both level- and configuration-average resolution return ion fractions that agree within 5-20%. The calculations probe the impact of including final-charge-state-resolved branching ratios for inner shell ionization which result in multi-ionization events from successive Auger cascades. Omission of these branching ratios is shown to have large impacts on the ionization balance. The calculated cross sections will be provided on Zenodo.

paper.title: Transient subtraction method: An alternative approach for variance reduction in dissipative particle dynamics
paper.summary: The efficient and accurate computation of transport coefficients remains a numerical challenge in dissipative particle dynamics (DPD), which can require substantial sampling to control statistical uncertainty. We extend recent results obtained in Langevin dynamics to consider the transient subtraction method for reducing the variance of transport coefficient estimations in DPD. The system is initialised by perturbing equilibrium samples, and its relaxation towards equilibrium is monitored under the reference dynamics. A reference trajectory, initialised at equilibrium and driven by the same Brownian noise, provides a control variate for the transient response. We apply the transient subtraction method to the computation of the mobility and the shear viscosity in a Lennard-Jones fluid in DPD. The shear viscosity is obtained from the time-integrated response of a Fourier observable associated with the longitudinal velocity. Numerical comparisons with the naive transient estimator show that the transient subtraction method reduces the variance at various integration times, and the reduction is more pronounced with a higher friction coefficient. These results indicate that the transient subtraction method is able to improve the statistical precision of transport coefficient estimations in DPD and reduce the number of trajectories needed to attain a prescribed standard error.

paper.title: Stroh--Hamiltonian Framework for Modeling Incompressible Poroelastic Materials
paper.summary: The Stroh sextic formalism, developed by Stroh, offers a compelling framework for representing the equilibrium equations in anisotropic elasticity. This approach has proven particularly effective for studying multilayered structures and time-harmonic problems, owing to its ability to seamlessly integrate physical constraints into the analysis. By recognizing that the Stroh formalism aligns with the canonical Hamiltonian structure, this work extends its application to Biot's poroelasticity, focusing on scenarios where the solid material is incompressible and there is no fluid pressure gradient. The study introduces a novel Hamiltonian-based approach to analyze such systems, offering deeper insights into the interplay between solid incompressibility and fluid-solid coupling. A key novelty lies in the derivation of canonical equations under these constraints, enabling clearer interpretations of reversible poroelastic behavior. However, the framework assumes perfectly drained conditions and neglects dissipative effects, which limits its applicability to fully realistic scenarios involving energy loss or complex fluid dynamics. Despite this limitation, the work provides a foundational step toward understanding constrained poroelastic systems and paves the way for future extensions to more general cases, including dissipative and nonlinear regimes.

paper.title: A closed-form design rule for photonic hopfions of arbitrary order
paper.summary: Topological textures of light are robust against perturbation and are emerging as carriers of information and probes of light-matter interaction. The most intricate of them, the photonic hopfion, in which the loops of different polarization states are linked, has so far been assembled from chosen superpositions of laser modes, with weights set by hand or found by numerical optimization. Here we replace this search with a design rule. Two scalar beams, an optical vortex of order $\ell$ and a field with n dark rings, propagate in closed form, and their phases on one plane are the two masks of a metasurface that controls two orthogonal polarizations. Although a beam, unlike the closed spaces of topology, extends to infinity, we prove that it is a hopfion of order $n\ell$ whenever three algebraic conditions on the ring coefficients and the vortex order hold, and that the polarization loops of every state that the far field does not reach then link exactly $n\ell$ times; each condition guards against one way in which the topology can escape. The order is thus chosen on paper and the device follows directly, without optimization. In scalar simulation, one terahertz metasurface geometry produces hopfions up to order nine, and a full-wave simulation of the complete first-order device preserves its topology. The rule applies to any platform that shapes the phases of two orthogonal polarizations.

paper.title: Shock wave transmission across solid-water interfaces in underwater electrical foil explosions
paper.summary: The transmission of shock waves generated by underwater electrical foil explosions across solid materials with varying acoustic impedances and thicknesses is investigated. Copper foils with thicknesses of 10 and 18 $μ$m are exploded on planar substrates of aluminum, copper, and 3D-printed PLA with thicknesses up to 5 mm using a multi-gigawatt pulsed-power electrical discharge. The resulting shocks are visualized in water using high-speed shadowgraphy at 5 million frames per second, while high-resolution fiber optic hydrophone measurements provide direct quantitative measurements of shock strength after transmission through the impedance-mismatched materials. One-dimensional magnetohydrodynamic simulations are used to reproduce the foil explosion dynamics and provide insight into the thermodynamic, acoustic, and electrical properties of the foil during the explosion. The results show that shock transmission is governed not only by the impedance mismatch at the solid--water interface but also by the finite thickness and dynamic response of the supporting material. These findings provide a quantitative framework for understanding and controlling shock transmission in underwater electrical foil explosions and establish the feasibility and limitations of using solid substrates as structural supports in complex shock-generating geometries.

paper.title: A $θ$-implicit hybrid particle-in-cell algorithm for kinetic simulations of magnetized plasmas
paper.summary: Hybrid particle-in-cell (PIC) models with kinetic ions and an inertialess electron fluid are widely used to simulate magnetized plasmas at ion scales, but explicit time advances are constrained by the whistler-wave CFL condition $\dt \propto Δx^2$, and the sub-cycling and artificial dissipation used to mitigate it carry accumulating costs. We present a $θ$-implicit hybrid PIC algorithm, implemented in the open-source GPU-capable code WarpX, in which fields and particles are advanced as a single nonlinear system solved by a particle-suppressed Jacobian-free Newton--Krylov method: the particles are nonlinearly eliminated, the electric field of the generalized Ohm's law is the sole unknown, and mass matrices remove all particle operations from the linear iterations. The electron pressure is advanced inside the nonlinear solve, and the scheme satisfies a discrete energy law whose single dissipation term vanishes at $θ= 1/2$ and damps only temporally under-resolved modes for $θ> 1/2$. The advance reproduces parallel and perpendicular wave dispersion including the ion Bernstein modes, conserves total energy to machine roundoff where the explicit advance heats secularly, does not develop the cold-beam finite-grid instability, and reproduces the $m=0$ instability of a Bennett pinch in RZ geometry. We conclude with 3D simulations of a field-reversed configuration initialized from a Grad--Shafranov equilibrium, comparing the explicit and implicit advances on the growth of the tilt instability and the preservation of trapped magnetic flux.

paper.title: A wider state, not wider arithmetic, for single-precision time integration
paper.summary: Single precision (FP32) halves the memory and data movement of double precision (FP64), and on accelerators is often several times faster. Its rounding errors are harmless except in the stored state. A modified equation for Runge-Kutta methods in Shu-Osher form and linear multistep methods separates the rounding of the stored state, a forcing proportional to $1/Δt$, from truncation and from right-hand-side rounding, which sets a $Δt$-independent floor. We bound this forcing for strong-stability-preserving schemes and identify two mechanisms that keep its sign fixed, so it accumulates as a bias: past a turnaround step, refining the step increases the error, in FP64 as in FP32. For a model oscillator the analysis predicts the floor and the FP32-to-FP64 ratios of turnaround step and minimum error within 30%. Our remedy needs no FP64 arithmetic: each state variable is stored as the unevaluated sum of two FP32 numbers, updated with error-free transformations, while every right-hand-side evaluation stays in FP32. Unlike compensated summation, it needs no rewriting of the scheme. In model problems from geophysical flow, mechanical dynamics and celestial mechanics, with five Runge-Kutta and multistep schemes, it restores design-order convergence to the floor. In large-eddy simulations of a high-lift airplane wing on three refined grids, up to 544 million cells, with time steps $Δt$, $Δt/2$ and $Δt/4$, FP32 overpredicts the lift by 2.1, 4.5 and 7.7%, while the two-float lift agrees with FP64 within 0.3% on every grid, and on graphics processing units the production solver runs 1.6 to 2.7 times faster than FP64.

paper.title: Mueller Matrix Decomposition for a General Rotating Compensator Ellipsometer
paper.summary: This work develops a Mueller matrix decomposition that factors a nondepolarizing Mueller matrix $M$ into three components $M = T_1 D T_2$, where the elements $D$, which correspond to a diagonal Jones matrix, are separated from rotations and circular diattenuation $T_1, T_2$. This decomposition is employed to calibrate a prototype reflective rotating-compensator ellipsometer designed to operate using extreme ultraviolet (EUV) radiation. This decomposition allows for the measurement of the full Mueller matrix of a sample without full knowledge of the compensators or the source polarization, while allowing for significant diattenuation and retardance for the optics. A generalization of the decomposition is developed for depolarizing Mueller matrices, and the technique is tested on reflection data collected on an Au mirror at $266$ nm.

paper.title: Interstellar and intergalactic medium in the ultraviolet band
paper.summary: This article presents an overview of key scientific challenges in the astrophysics and astrochemistry of the interstellar and intergalactic media. Addressing many of these challenges will become possible with the Russian space observatory Spektr-UF, which is currently being prepared for launch. The ultraviolet (UV) spectral range is critically important for studying the evolution of the Universe, as it contains fundamental absorption and emission lines of most chemical elements and the most important molecules. These lines make it possible to reliably determine the physical conditions and chemical composition of various astrophysical objects, as well as the characteristics of the processes occurring within them. The article examines the prospects for UV observations across a broad range of scientific problems, from investigating the epoch of helium reionization and the thermal history of the Universe to mapping ongoing star formation in galaxies. Dedicated sections address the study of the chemical evolution of galaxies at intermediate redshifts, the distribution of "hidden" baryons and metals, the small-scale structure of interstellar clouds, the physics of photodissociation regions and protoplanetary disks, and the modeling of UV emission from nebulae surrounding fast-moving pulsars. The high sensitivity and spectral resolution of the Spektr-UF instruments are expected to provide fundamentally new data across all these research areas, filling existing gaps in our understanding of the interstellar and intergalactic media.

paper.title: Mercury (Hg): a relativistic $N$-body simulation for Horndeski gravity
paper.summary: We present Mercury, a relativistic $N$-body code for cosmological simulations in the $α$-basis formulation of Horndeski gravity. Mercury extends a particle-mesh scheme by incorporating the dynamics of the additional scalar degree of freedom and the corresponding modified Einstein equations, expressed in terms of the time-dependent functions $α_{\rm K}, α_{\rm B}, α_{\rm M}, α_{\rm T}$ and the effective Planck mass $M_*^2$. This generalises our previous implementation of Horndeski subclass models, namely $k$-essence and kinetic gravity braiding (KGB), to the general linear Horndeski $α$-basis. The code evolves the additional scalar degree of freedom and its effective stress--energy tensor alongside the nonlinear matter and metric fields, so that nonlinear structure formation sources the scalar-field evolution and feeds back on the gravitational potentials. Through its interface with hi_class, Mercury supports both phenomenological $α$-function parametrisations and covariant Horndeski theories; we demonstrate the latter using nKGB, the Cubic Galileon, and Brans--Dicke models. We validate the implementation against hi_class in the linear regime and recover the expected nonlinear $k$-essence and KGB limits. For the luminal Horndeski models considered here, we show how a running effective Planck mass generates gravitational slip through the scalar anisotropic stress and modifies the friction terms governing the vector and tensor metric perturbations. The evolution of $M_*^2$ also modifies the normalisation and scale dependence of the effective dark-energy density contrast, leaving a corresponding imprint on its power spectrum. The present framework provides an intermediate step towards nonlinear Horndeski simulations, in which nonlinear scalar self-interactions and screening effects can be incorporated consistently within the same relativistic framework.

paper.title: Lagrangian Irreversibility in Stratified Turbulence
paper.summary: Stable stratification reorganizes turbulence, suppressing vertical motion and altering the balance between vortical and strain-dominated flow structures. How these changes affect the temporal asymmetry of kinetic-energy exchange along fluid-particle trajectories remains incompletely understood. Using direct numerical simulations of homogeneous Boussinesq turbulence, we investigate Lagrangian power statistics across four local velocity-gradient topology classes and three nonzero stratification strengths, with an unstratified reference case. With increasing stratification, the global power variance decreases while the standardized skewness becomes more negative, indicating enhanced asymmetry despite weaker fluctuations. Conditioning on local topology reveals distinct responses: axial-strain-dominated regions exhibit the most negative total-power skewness at all stratification strengths, whereas biaxial-strain-dominated regions change sign from positive to negative under stratification. Horizontal and vertical component powers also respond differently, revealing directional dependence. Among the dynamical contributions to power, the pressure contribution, nearly symmetric in the unstratified case, becomes more negatively skewed with increasing stratification. Energy-conditioned pressure statistics further indicate altered pressure-mediated energy redistribution. Finally, tracer persistence-time distributions exhibit exponential tails, with time scales that differ across topology classes and respond differently to stratification. Increasing stratification is thus accompanied by three concurrent changes: enhanced asymmetry of Lagrangian power, modified energy redistribution by pressure, and altered temporal sampling of local flow structures by tracers. These co-occurring signatures characterize the response to stratification, though their causal relations remain to be established.

paper.title: Neuromorphic Camera for Multi-Target Pointing Acquisition and Tracking in Free Space Optical Communication
paper.summary: Pointing, Acquisition, and Tracking (PAT) in Free-Space Optical Communication (FSOC) applications must achieve both low jitter and a large Field of View (FoV) to support beacon acquisition and multi-target tracking. While conventional frame-based sensors provide the necessary angular coverage, their performance is limited by latency, available frame-rate, and motion blur. This work explores and demonstrates the application of an event-based vision sensor for PAT tasks in FSOC. The system employs a neuromorphic sensor that asynchronously records brightness changes (events) with microsecond-level temporal resolution. The main contribution of this paper is a comparative analysis of event-based tracking algorithms for the simultaneous acquisition and tracking of multiple optical beacons that operate directly on this asynchronous stream. The performance of these strategies is validated on an experimental dataset representing realistic operational conditions for dynamic High-Altitude Platform (HAP) and Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) networks. The analysis compares key metrics, such as tracking accuracy and processing latency, under various signal-to-background conditions.

paper.title: Counterexample-driven autonomous research with application to excess radiated energy in a Z-pinch
paper.summary: Recent breakthroughs in artificial-intelligence-assisted mathematics show that open-ended machine search can outperform human mathematicians, yet transferring this paradigm to physics requires refactoring the research workflow. We introduce Simjecture, an open-source framework in which language-model agents pursue human-defined physical conjectures. The framework tackles two central challenges in this transfer: first, because physics is empirical and no model is final, it structures inquiry around counterexample-driven falsification and prospective hypothesis repair; second, because physical theories must interact with the real world, it uses computational physics as an executable testbed while separating the qualification of numerical instruments from scientific claim review so solvers and diagnostics can be adapted within a recorded investigation. We apply the framework in an 82.6 h investigation to tackle the long-standing problem of radiated energy exceeding the imploding-shell kinetic energy in a Z-pinch. The investigation reveals competing effects of energy conversion, retention, and release timing. Stronger coherent helical deformation increases resistive conversion while reducing radiation and increasing retained energy. A broader trailing-plasma profile delays the later radiation maximum and recovers much of its early bolometric deficit, with a spectral response that changes during the pulse. These results provide new insight into energy conversion in high-energy-density plasma physics and demonstrate a new paradigm for physics research.

paper.title: Computational performance versus numerical accuracy in the acoustic terms of weakly-compressible SPH
paper.summary: Accurate computation of the acoustic terms in weakly-compressible SPH, including the equation of state, its inverse, and the evaluation of the local speed of sound, is essential to ensure energy conservation, robust solid boundary conditions, and correct open boundary behavior. In the classic Cole's equation of state, using values of the polytropic constant $γ\ne 1$ can lead to significant precision loss, particularly when computations are performed in single precision, as is common in GPU implementations. We extend here our previous results on the optimal choice of state variable by introducing a new higher-precision form for all three acoustic terms, denoted \texttt{explog}, and assess its numerical accuracy and computational performance across a variety of devices and test cases. We find that the new form evaluates the acoustic terms with a maximum ULP of~2 for arguments less than $0.125$, and has higher errors in less than 1\% of the arguments larger than the threshold. Combined with a rewritten expression of the pressure at solid boundary particles in the ``dummy'' model, it provides consistently more accurate results, maintaining deviations from the reference pressure profile to below 2\%, even in presence of a rough bottom terrain. Computationally, the new formulation is also faster than the naive one on GPU, and only marginally slower on CPU.

paper.title: The Nonlinear Physics and Statistical Field Theory of Twilight Clouds: Hovering Dynamics and Dynamic Inertia Emergence
paper.summary: Twilight clouds are small, optically faint warm clouds whose droplets fluctuate between haze and activated growth. We develop a nonequilibrium statistical field theory linking this regime to cloud-field organization through Köhler microphysics, supersaturation transport, and turbulent mixing. At parcel level, supersaturation rapidly tracks slow droplet growth with a finite lag. Mixing-induced supersaturation removal drives a saddle-node bifurcation, shifting the activation threshold and supporting intermittent hovering under turbulent fluctuations. Starting from turbulent transport of supersaturation coupled to droplet growth, we derive a droplet-supersaturation field system and formulate it within the Martin-Siggia-Rose framework. A Gurari-type variational reduction inspired by polaron theory eliminates the fast bath. Turbulence dresses the slow droplet field, shrinks the forbidden zone below the equilibrium curve, and raises the mixing threshold required to suppress activation. Each droplet population induces a screened supersaturation halo that couples neighboring cloud elements; its delayed adjustment generates dynamic inertia and temporally correlated noise. The resulting nonlinear, non-Markovian pseudoparabolic stochastic equation has a bounded frozen-background response at short wavelengths. Its long-wave coupling amplifies contrasts where the dressed slow manifold turns downward. Comparisons with the parent two-field system show that a spatially correlated Markovian closure preserves droplet-radius distributions and cloudlet organization. Near the activation fold, restoring residual-bath fluctuation memory improves recurrent-hovering frequency and patch extent without recalibrating the drift or fitting a correlation time. More broadly, the framework identifies how slow fields acquire interactions and inertia through the relaxing, diffusive environments they modify.

paper.title: Perturbation-Based Reconstruction of Depth-Resolved OCT Attenuation without Requiring a Fully Decayed Signal Tail
paper.summary: Depth-resolved attenuation in optical coherence tomography (OCT) can provide quantitative optical contrast beyond structural imaging. However, conventional reconstruction methods can be biased when the OCT signal does not fully decay within the imaging range or when the distal signal tail is dominated by noise or residual reflections from distal sample or support interfaces. Here, we present a perturbation-based Beer-Lambert framework that combines a zeroth-order exponential estimate with a first-order correction, reducing reliance on the unreliable distal signal tail below the current depth. Numerical A-line simulations, Monte Carlo modeling, multilayer silicone-dye-TiO2 phantoms, and ex vivo bovine retina experiments were used to evaluate the method under finite-depth and heterogeneous imaging conditions. The numerical A-line tests showed reduced depth-dependent error against prescribed attenuation profiles; the Monte Carlo comparisons showed less distal drift relative to model-defined benchmarks, while the phantom profiles were compared with separately acquired single-layer OCT calibration values. In a Monte Carlo component test that withheld vessel-mask and vessel-boundary information from reconstruction and used that information only for post hoc evaluation, the first-order correction recovered 61% of the segmentation-informed target vessel contrast and reduced vessel ROI mean absolute error by 65% relative to the fixed zeroth-order baseline. These results suggest that perturbation-based reconstruction may provide a practical approach for depth-resolved reconstruction of effective OCT attenuation when the fully decayed A-line condition is not satisfied.

paper.title: Structure of energy flux densities in Earth's magnetotail reconnection regions: Bridging simulation and observation
paper.summary: Magnetic reconnection is important in both space and laboratory contexts because it changes the topology of magnetic fields and converts magnetic energy into particle energies. Establishing where this energy conversion occurs is critical for understanding how reconnection partitions energy. Using a novel machine learning approach based on simulations that explicitly identifies the separatrix regions for the first time, the partition of energy flux densities within the magnetic reconnection site is evaluated through statistical study of magnetotail reconnection events observed in situ. The separatrices are found to have the largest electron energy flux densities, roughly twice those in the exhaust, and Poynting flux densities about four times those in the inflows, whereas typical ion enthalpy flux densities are largest in the exhaust. The separatrices are therefore sites of intense electron and electromagnetic energy transport, although their small thickness means that the exhaust may still carry most of the total energy flux.

paper.title: Learning the Entropic Relaxation: Stable Coarse-Grid Emulation with Neural Discrete Equilibrium
paper.summary: The ability to emulate complicated and computationally-expensive physical systems in an efficient and stable manner is a popular motivation for scientific machine learning (SciML). Stable numerical solvers tend to be computationally expensive, as they attempt to resolve small (spatial and temporal) scales that receive and dissipate spectral energy. Learned coarse-grid forecasters remove the dissipative channel, allowing unresolved frequencies to re-emerge as grid-scale noise (aliasing). In this paper, we use the Neural Discrete Equilibrium (NeurDE) method to explore stable emulation at extremely coarse grids, demonstrating physically-principled control over entropy dynamics that reinforces the physical system's dissipative mechanism. Entropically-stabilized NeurDE produces stable long-time rollouts for thousands of forecasting steps on large Reynolds number turbulent flows ($\mathrm{Re}=100{,}000$) with very coarse grids (down to $\mathbb{R}^{16\times16}$). At these very coarse grid scales, entropically-stabilized NeurDE can be more stable than even our stabilized data-generation numerical method.

paper.title: Reconstructing Rayleigh--Bénard flows from temperature-only measurements using the Ensemble Kalman Filter
paper.summary: Reconstructing the full state of a multiscale chaotic system from observations of only a subset of its degrees of freedom is a central problem in data assimilation. Turbulent Rayleigh--Bénard convection offers a paradigmatic example, for which Charney conjectured that temperature measurements alone should suffice to determine the velocity field. Synchronization-based methods such as nudging and direct replacement nonetheless fail in chaotic regimes, because they require the measurement of the determining modes of the system, a set to which the velocity belongs but the temperature does not. Here we show that the Ensemble Kalman Filter (EnKF), equipped with a proper inflation scheme, removes this asymmetry by exploiting the flow-dependent cross-covariances between temperature and vorticity, and recovers the velocity from noisy and spatio-temporally sparse temperature data alone. We assess the filter in two chaotic regimes of two-dimensional bulk convection by means of a scale-by-scale spectral analysis. When the whole temperature field is observed, both fields synchronize with the true state at all resolved scales, with the temperature estimate becoming even more accurate than the measurements themselves for sufficiently frequent observations. Equispaced observation networks preserve this full-spectrum synchronization down to a threshold density, below which only the largest scales remain synchronized, as also happens when observations are confined to a subdomain. We conclude that Charney's conjecture is numerically verified in two-dimensional turbulent convection when the assimilation is performed using a properly calibrated EnKF.

paper.title: Generalized Lorentz Framework for Active Semiconductor Quantum Surface Plasmonics
paper.summary: Nanostructured semiconductors provide an actively tunable platform for light-matter interactions across a broad spectral range. As feature sizes shrink to the deep nanoscale (~10 nm scale), nonclassical carrier dynamics and surface plasmonic responses become prominent, creating substantial challenges for a rigorous and efficient theoretical treatment. Here we develop a generalized Lorentz framework for quantum surface plasmonics in nanostructured semiconductors with arbitrary energymomentum dispersion relations. The framework enables efficient quantitative treatment of carrier nonlocality, carrier surface accumulation and depletion, and nonlocal damping in three-dimensional semiconductor nanostructures, under electrical tuning and across a wide range of doping densities. Building on this framework, we further establish a rigorous quasinormal-mode analysis that provides transparent physical insight into complex surface plasmonic responses of multiscale semiconductor structures. We demonstrate electrically controlled deep-nanoscale carrier accumulation and depletion in a semiconductor nanoantenna, leading to pronounced plasmonic-response modulation that can be interpreted in terms of eigenmode shifts, creation, and annihilation. By quantifying and linking complex nonclassical carrier dynamics with plasmonic eigenmodes, our work establishes a comprehensive quantitative framework for active semiconductor quantum surface plasmonics and will foster the convergence of electronics and photonics at the deep nanoscale.

paper.title: Comparison of models for dynamical structures of solar plasma
paper.summary: Possible mechanisms of generation of dynamical plasma structures are associated with the Schwarzschild criterion for convective instability and with excess energy (heat, magnetic): due to the superadiabatic temperature gradient, the overheated plasma starts to rise. In the framework of Navier-Stokes MHD equations, the complete system of equations for the full axisymmetric plasma model includes equations for the stream function, the azimuthal velocity component, the density change, the flow function of poloidal magnetic field, and the azimuthal component of the magnetic field. Within the framework of ideal hydrodynamics, the simplest plasma model is applicable to the initial stage of generation of plasma structures. In this case, rigorous analytical solutions are constructed from blocks. Within the framework of ideal hydrodynamics, some intermediate model - the refined model considers rotating plasma at the growth stage. In this case, some unidirectional differential rotation occurs. The full model studies the development of structures as rotating plasma from the very beginning to the highest development stage. The velocity field is adjusted to boundary conditions. Velocity components change in a coordinated manner. The stationary axisymmetric ambient magnetic field and its gradients have little effect on the plasma structure and velocity field. The movement structures for all models are similar. Radial flows converge towards the axis at the bottom, and there is an outflow to the periphery near the top of the plasma structure. The maximum vertical velocity component is reached at the center of the axis. Applications of these models to solar structures, including jets, are discussed.

paper.title: Machine-Learned Interatomic Potential for the Mo-S-Al-O System
paper.summary: We develop a machine-learned neuroevolution potential (NEP) for the Mo-S-Al-O system, targeting MoS$_2$ heteroepitaxy on c-plane sapphire, $α$-Al$_2$O$_3$(0001). The potential is trained on 63,611 PBE+D3 structures distilled from about 1.1 million curated density-functional-theory (DFT) configurations, using an energy-difference loss function that directly targets interfacial and orientation-dependent energies. On held-out data, the energy and force errors are 29 meV/atom and 0.23 eV/$\mathring{A}$. Validated against DFT on a suite of physical properties, the NEP reproduces the lattice constants within 0.3 %, the elastic constants within 17 %, the phonon dispersions with mean deviations below 2.5%, and the surface energies within 1.3 %. At the MoS$_2$/sapphire interface, it reproduces the adhesion energy minimum within 0.8 %, the interfacial energy within 2.2 % and the most stable orientation of the monolayer. It preserves the DFT-predicted energetic ordering of edges, point defects (Spearman $ρ$ = 0.995) and mirror-twin boundaries ($ρ$ = 1.0), and reproduces tilt grain-boundary energies within 8 % ($ρ$ = 0.98) and stacking-fault energy barriers within 14 %. The resulting potential enables future studies of the atomic-scale mechanisms of defect formation in two-dimensional heteroepitaxy.

paper.title: Designing turbulence through hierarchies
paper.summary: Turbulence is defined by a set of emergent and singular phenomena: a constant-flux energy cascade, intermittency, a dissipation rate that survives the vanishing of viscosity, and the spontaneous loss of determinism of the inviscid limit. Which physical ingredients produce them remains unclear, because in fluids they always come together with incompressibility, spatial structure and vortex dynamics. Here we show that a hierarchy of inertia, coupled by the purely geometric nonlinearity of rigid constraints, is enough. A planar chain of rigid pendula whose lengths and masses decrease geometrically, coupled only through nearest-neighbor constraints, develops a far-from-equilibrium cascade that replaces thermal equipartition, with statistically local and time-irreversible energy transfer despite intrinsically nonlocal coupling. Its fluctuations are intermittent, yet self-similarity is restored by a hidden scale symmetry. As the viscosity vanishes, the dissipation rate saturates at a finite value, and thermal noise consistent with fluctuation-dissipation balance is amplified from the smallest to the largest scales within a fraction of a large-scale period.
